data.cultural_impact: Avellina is a name with deep roots in the Italian cultural landscape. It was once a common name in many regions of Italy, particularly in central and southern parts of the country. The name has a lovely, gentle ring to it, and it evokes images of nature, warmth, and the simple joys of rural life. In Italy, saints are often venerated in the places where they lived and died, and St. Avellina is no exception. The town of Montefiascone in Lazio, where she is said to have lived, is still a popular pilgrimage site for those seeking spiritual guidance and healing.
data.spiritual_significance: Avellina's name is rooted in the Christian tradition, and it represents the humility and devotion of a devoted follower of Christ. The name 'avellana' means 'little bird,' which is a beautiful metaphor for the small and vulnerable creatures that are often overlooked and cherished by God. In the same way, St. Avellina was a humble and devoted woman who lived a simple life in a small Italian town. Her name serves as a reminder that even the smallest among us can have a profound impact on the world, and that God loves and cares for all of his creatures, no matter how insignificant they may seem. Avellina's life and legacy inspire those who bear her name to live humbly, with love and devotion, and to cherish all of God's creations.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Avellina: Devotion and strength from the mountain of God. A name inspired by St. Avellina, patroness of difficult pregnancies and infertility, embodying the hope and resilience in overcoming life's challenges.
